compiled_state.title: As a reviewer agent, cycle-end rulings use bounded BLOCK/DEFER/DROP enums so outcomes are deterministic and machine-readable
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Story

As a reviewer agent, cycle-end rulings use bounded BLOCK/DEFER/DROP enums so that outcomes are deterministic, machine-readable, and consistent between local and CI environments.

## Done Definitions

- [ ] `code-reviewer-arbiter.md` rewrites the ruling schema: output contains exactly one of `BLOCK`, `DEFER`, or `DROP` per finding group; no free-form verdict strings
- [ ] Per-Finding Processing Protocol implemented: arbiter processes findings one at a time, assigns ruling per finding, then aggregates; no batch short-circuits that skip individual finding evaluation
- [ ] BLOCK-gate uses AND-logic: a `BLOCK` ruling is only issued when ALL of the following are true: (a) severity is critical or important, (b) defense was rejected or absent, (c) cycle ≤ max_cycles
- [ ] CoVe soft-cap fallback: when cycle count exceeds `max_cycles`, arbiter must emit `DEFER` (not `BLOCK`) for remaining unresolved findings; behavior documented in ruling schema
- [ ] `dso_ci_review/arbiter.py` and its test suite updated to consume new BLOCK/DEFER/DROP schema; old SUSTAIN/ACCEPT/DOWNGRADE strings removed; CI tests pass
- [ ] ADR 0013 (`docs/adr/0013-verifier-severity-authority.md`) reviewed; if its four-prong exception scope conflicts with new rulings, an ADR amendment or addendum is filed as a ticket (not in this story's scope to resolve, but must be identified)
- [ ] Arbiter output includes `schema_version` field matching the cycle-ledger schema version convention
- [ ] Existing arbiter tests (in `tests/`) updated or replaced; no test references old verdict strings

## Considerations

- [Consumer impact] `dso_ci_review/arbiter.py` currently asserts old schema fields — verify with `grep -r "SUSTAIN\|ACCEPT\|DOWNGRADE" dso_ci_review/`; update all assertion sites
- [ADR 0013 check] Read `docs/adr/0013-verifier-severity-authority.md` before implementing BLOCK-gate logic; the four-prong exception scope may constrain which findings the arbiter can BLOCK
- [Enum exhaustiveness] Add a schema-level assertion that every finding in the arbiter output has exactly one of BLOCK/DEFER/DROP; fail loudly if an unknown ruling appears
- [Escalation policy] Escalate when blocked

comments.body: Consideration (from S2 completion-verifier): When implementing arbiter cycle-count logic, add reader behavior for cycle-ledger.json: (a) load ARTIFACTS_DIR/cycle-ledger.json if present, (b) if reconstruction_gaps=true, log a warning to stderr and treat ledger-absent cycles as 'unknown' rather than assuming cycle 0, (c) use this cycle count for BLOCK-gate and CoVe soft-cap logic. The write side (S2) sets reconstruction_gaps correctly — S3 must implement the corresponding reader path.

comments.body: ADR 0013 review (task 16f1): No conflict for BLOCK or DEFER — both are merge-gate/continuation signals that do NOT modify any finding's severity field; Rule 11 is not triggered. DROP ruling overlaps structurally with the verifier's DROP (ADR 0013 prong 2), but ADR 0013 only authorizes code-reviewer-verifier, not code-reviewer-arbiter. Filed ticket 7edb-c652-b675-41a4 to amend ADR 0013 to explicitly cover code-reviewer-arbiter DROP authority. Amendment is not blocking this story.
